newsitem.title: USA: US expects final decision on EU beef ban this fall.
newsitem.headline: US expects final decision on EU beef ban this fall.

text.p: A final World Trade Organization decision on a beef trade dispute between the U.S. and the European Union is not expected before sometime this fall, U.S. officials said today.
"The case will not be final... until sometime in September roughly," U.S. Trade Representative Charlene Barshefsky told the Senate Agriculture Committee.

Last month, a WTO dispute settlement panel issued a preliminary report which said the EU's ban on beef produced with artificial growth hormones violated its commitments under the Uruguay Round trade pact, Barshefsky told the panel.
If the final report upholds that conclusion--as is expected--EU officials plan to appeal, Barshefsky said.

That will drag out a final decision on the matter until at least September. However, delays much beyond that point are not expected because of the timetable contained in the WTO dispute settlement process for reaching a final decision, she said.

The value of U.S. meat exports blocked by the EU was estimated at $100 million in 1989, when the ban first went into effect. However, the US beef industry now places lost sales closer to $200 million annually.
U.S. Agriculture Secretary Dan Glickman repeated today that U.S. wants the EU to open its market to U.S. hormone-treated beef rather than pay compensation.

The bulk of U.S. beef comes from cattle that have been injected with artificial growth hormones to make them put on weight faster. Many Europeans have a strong aversion to the practice, although most scientists agree the practice is safe.
